name: Escitalopram
executiveSummary: SSRI (S-enantiomer of citalopram). Adult: **10 mg PO/day** (range **5–20 mg**; max **20 mg/day**). Elderly: usual max **10 mg/day** (QT). Adolescents ≥12 y (by country): **10 mg**, max **20 mg**. Suicide ideation risk early on.
indications:
## Indications

- Major depression; generalized anxiety; panic (labels).

## Precautions

- QT prolongation — do not exceed maxima; avoid other QT+; ECG if at risk.
- Same SSRI alerts: suicide early/dose change, serotonergic, hyponatremia, bleeding.
- Reduce to **10 mg** max in >65 y on many labels.

> 10 mg escitalopram ≈ 20 mg citalopram (approximate).

adulto.dose: Start **10 mg PO/day**; if needed **20 mg** after ≥1 week. Elderly/hepatic: start **5 mg**, max **10 mg/day**.
adulto.administration: PO once daily, morning or night.

pediatrico.dose: ≥12 y (if authorized): **10 mg/day**; max **20 mg**. <12 y: not routine / specialist.

neonatal.notes: Neonatal adaptation syndrome if prenatal exposure.

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, insomnia, fatigue, sexual dysfunction, sweating; long QT at high doses; hyponatremia.
